title: One transformer layer: residual stream, Q/K/V projections, norm, and feed-forward
why: It shows the layer's dataflow and tensor shapes that the prose introduces in sequence: x, the three projection matrices, q/k/v, residual addition, layer norm, and the feed-forward block.
nodes: x: residual stream vector, length d_model
W_Q, W_K, W_V: each d_model by d_k
q = x W_Q, k = x W_K, v = x W_V: each length d_k
feed-forward: two linear layers with inner width typically 4 times d_model
notes: Flow runs left to right along the residual stream. Label x as d_model; label each weight matrix as d_model x d_k; label q, k, v as d_k. Show that the same W matrices apply to every token, so n tokens yield n queries, n keys, and n values. Show the residual addition as a bypass path around the sublayer. Note that the original 2017 paper placed LayerNorm after the residual addition, while most later models moved it before the sublayer. The feed-forward block is applied per position independently, with inner width typically 4 times d_model. | Flow left to right. Rows of S and A are queries i; columns are keys j. Label n tokens, d_model, h heads, and d_k = d_model/h. The scaling factor sqrt(d_k) sits between S and softmax. The multi-head branch splits the projected Q/K/V width d_model into h parallel d_k-wide attention computations, then concatenates back to d_model before W_O. A small inset can show the chapter's softmax example: scores 2, 1, 0 give exponentials 7.389, 2.718, 1.000, sum 11.107, shares 0.665, 0.245, 0.090, and with values (1,0), (0,1), (1,1) the output is (0.755, 0.335). | Two-panel comparison. Left panel: dependency depth vs total work; recurrence is a chain of n steps, attention is a short chain over a wide n^2 score matrix. Right panel: memory footprint per head (34 GB), all heads (>1 TB), and available unified memory (111.5 GB), with tiling as the flow that avoids materializing the full matrix. All quantities are from the chapter: n=130,659, d_model=4096, h=32, d_k=128, 1.71×10^10 pairs, 2.8×10^14 FLOPs / 1.4×10^14 MACs, 2.2×10^12 MACs, ratio ≈64, 34 GB, 111.5 GB. | No axes; the flow is q_t into scores against the t cached keys, mask before softmax so exp(-inf)=0 and each row sums only over the past, then the weighted sum reads the t cached values. At step t only q_t is computed; K and V for earlier positions are reused from the KV cache. The cache grows with t and is what limits concurrency: the engine runs four streams against a shared pool of 262,144 positions with a 32,768-token reply budget. Measured on this pair, one stream decodes at 59.1 tok/s and four concurrent streams aggregate 106.2 tok/s, a 1.80 multiplier, against a shared 273 GB/s LPDDR5X memory ceiling. Prefill is compute-bound at 39,237 tok/s, with 95.9% of prompt tokens served from the prefix cache, removing 313 seconds of prefill over the sampled window.
